componentMapping: chemistry > periodic-table > general crystal-lattice structure example (silicate mineral, covalent network crystal) -- bonus candidate beyond the named metal/nonmetal/metalloid/noble-gas gap; also a generally reusable "real mineral crystal system" asset for molecules-and-bonding lattice comparisons
underlyingStructureData: Ball-and-stick alpha-quartz (SiO2) crystal model, per-entry description: "3D models (created by OpenSCAD, fully printable) for creating alpha quartz crystal. Basic atom model can be used to crease an atom with any number of bonds at any angle..."
creator: DemoniWaari (demoniwaari@gmail.com)
attributionText: Not legally required. Recommended credit: "Alpha Quartz", NIH 3D (3d.nih.gov, entry 3DPX-008115), by DemoniWaari. CC0 1.0.
redistributionStatus: Unrestricted (CC0 public domain dedication). Confirmed via NIH 3D entry page license badge linking to the CC0 1.0 deed.
downloadedVariant: Molecule_print_0_NIH3D.glb (the entry's .glb output; .stl/.wrl/.x3d/.scad variants also exist on the entry and were not downloaded)

validation.generator: https://github.com/mikedh/trimesh (STL-to-GLB conversion of a 3D-printable ball-and-stick unit-cell model, not an authored-for-web asset)

approxBoundingBox.units: millimeters (source was authored as a physical 3D-print unit-cell model; not normalized to app scene units)

reviewNote: Structural GLB validation and license verification only. Single untextured mesh, no per-atom material assigned by source (converted from a 3D-print STL, fused into one mesh rather than separate atom/bond nodes) -- unlike the app's existing RCSB-derived molecules (water.glb, glucose.glb etc.) which have per-atom CPK-colored materials, this file will need a material/re-coloring pass to match that language. File is comparatively large (5.1MB) for a single untextured mesh -- a decimation pass is recommended before integration. Not visually inspected in this pass; do not treat as PASS.
